data.title: Meta Plans to Sell 10 Million Wearable Devices in 2026
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing The Information, Meta Platforms plans to sell 10 million wearable devices in the second half of 2026 to expand its AI hardware lineup.

data.title: Fed Regional Employees Told to Expect Smaller Raises in 2027
data.description: According to Bloomberg, the Federal Reserve warned employees at its regional offices to expect lower pay increases in 2027, according to a memo viewed by Bloomberg News.

data.title: SEC's Brian Daly: Innovative ETF Reviews May Bring Sporadic Notices and Fine-Tuning
data.description: Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas wrote on X that SEC's Brian Daly discussed the comment period for innovative products. According to Odaily, Daly said new ETF ideas are often copied on the day they are submitted and that some issuers need to change their practices. He said major changes should not be expected, with notices and further adjustments likely to come incrementally.

data.title: Securitize Says Anthropic Token Holders Are Not Registered Shareholders, Product Was Not Endorsed
data.description:
Securitize said holders of its Anthropic tokenized stock are not registered Anthropic shareholders, and Anthropic did not sponsor, authorize or endorse the product.

According to Odaily, the tokenized stock launched on Securitize Stocks on Solana on Anthropic’s first day of trading. It is backed 1:1 by the underlying shares, with trades settled in USDC.

data.title: Ripple CLO Stuart Alderoty: Warren Won't Lead U.S. Crypto Policy
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Ripple Chief Legal Officer Stuart Alderoty said at the Capitol Crypto Forum, co-hosted by The Hill and The Block, that he does not expect Elizabeth Warren to lead U.S. crypto policy. If Warren becomes chair of the Senate Banking Committee, Alderoty expects her focus to be oversight and hearings, which could cause short-term disruption, while other lawmakers shape policy. Alderoty also chairs the National Cryptocurrency Association.

Alderoty said the Clarity Act is unlikely to be revived in the current Congress because of a crowded legislative calendar and the 2028 presidential election. Some provisions could be included in tax or other legislation, but he said the full bill is unlikely to secure enough committee support for a floor vote. He expects policy work to shift toward the SEC and CFTC, with coordination involving the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.

He said regulatory rulemaking can be sufficient and important even without market structure legislation, arguing that rules developed through public comment and data analysis would be harder for a future administration to reverse. He criticized former SEC Chair Gary Gensler for relying on enforcement rather than completing rulemaking. Alderoty also urged the industry to align its positions on DeFi, stablecoin rewards and token classification, saying crypto is a policy issue, not a political one.

data.title: Lina Khan's Approach Emerges in New York City Revenue-Share Deals
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Mayor Zohran Mamdani tapped former US antitrust enforcer Lina Khan for a top economic development role. Khan is shaping New York City's approach to promoting growth and hiring, including its revenue-share deals.

data.title: U.S. Energy Secretary Wright: Diesel Prices Would Be Lower If Europe Released Supply Like the U.S.
data.description: According to Jin10, U.S. Energy Secretary Wright said diesel prices would not be this high if Europe released supply as the United States has.

data.title: Robinhood Chain Launches Anthropic Stock Token ANT on Anthropic’s Listing Day
data.description: Robinhood Chain launched the Anthropic stock token ANT on the first day of Anthropic’s listing. According to Odaily, ANT joins more than 200 stock tokens already on the chain, giving users on-chain exposure to U.S. markets. Robinhood stock tokens are issued by Robinhood Assets (Jersey) Limited and are tokenized debt securities. They are not issued by the underlying stock companies and do not give holders ownership of, or related rights to, those stocks.

data.title: AI | Nscale-ByteDance Computing Deal Draws Scrutiny Under US Chip Curbs
data.description: Nscale Plc’s agreement to sell artificial intelligence computing capacity to ByteDance Ltd. will face greater regulatory scrutiny after the US moved to curb China’s access to American technology overseas, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: Offshore Chinese Yuan Falls to More Than One-Month Low as Dollar Rallies
data.description: According to Bloomberg, the offshore Chinese yuan fell to its weakest level in more than a month as the dollar rallied and risk appetite shrank.

data.title: Hedge Funds Dump AI Stocks at Record Pace as Money Rotates to Consumer Discretionary
data.description: Hedge funds sold roughly $20 billion in tech stocks over two weeks in October, with selling continuing into November at the fastest pace in at least a decade. The retreat erased net AI-stock purchases accumulated since early 2025 and left funds with their lowest ratio of bullish to bearish tech positions since tracking began in 2016, according to BeInCrypto, citing Goldman Sachs data. Nvidia reported record quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year over year, while Bank of America’s November survey found 52% of fund managers expect at least one major cloud company to cut AI spending within six months; 34% cited an AI bubble as the biggest market tail risk. Tech allocations saw their sharpest monthly reduction since 2006. Hedge funds’ strongest buying interest in the week ending November 12 was in consumer discretionary stocks; real estate and healthcare attracted buying in October, although healthcare saw renewed selling in November. Goldman described the activity as “more rotational.” Some funds are opening fresh short positions, while investors assess whether major AI spenders can turn infrastructure outlays into stronger profits; slower spending could pressure chipmakers and data-center suppliers.

data.title: Kushner: Trump Open to NATO Article 5-Like Security Guarantees for Ukraine
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said U.S. President Donald Trump is open to providing Ukraine with security guarantees similar to NATO's Article 5.

Speaking to reporters in Berlin, Kushner said the United States considers such guarantees “very, very important.” Article 5 treats an attack on one NATO member as an attack on all members.

Kushner said the guarantees must serve U.S. interests and be part of a broader security plan. He added that he believed Russia had accepted the concept that any security guarantees for Ukraine would be based on Article 5.

data.title: Ledger Probes Tampered Wallets in Berlin and Two Suspect Devices in Dubai as Investigators Trace Suspected $87 Million Theft
data.description: Ledger said it found tampered hardware wallets in Berlin and is investigating two possibly affected devices in Dubai. According to Odaily, Ledger said the devices are linked to the same incident it initially tracked in Southeast Asia. All confirmed devices had physical modifications intended to capture recovery phrases during setup. The investigation began after buyers from CryptoBilis, a distributor, reported losing funds, and on-chain investigators traced a suspected $87 million theft. Ledger said its chips and operating system have no defects and that devices purchased from ledger.com are unaffected. It advised people who bought devices in Berlin since January to transfer their funds to a new device using a new recovery phrase.

data.title: Netflix, Amazon and Fox Expected to Bid for 2030 Men's World Cup Rights; Disney Out
data.description: According to CNBC, Netflix, Amazon, YouTube and Fox are expected to bid for U.S. media rights to the 2030 men's World Cup before today's deadline, while Disney will not bid. Fox and Telemundo are the incumbent rights holders, and FIFA would prefer to sell the English- and Spanish-language rights to one buyer. Media companies can also bid for rights to the 2034 tournament. The winning offer could be around $1.5 billion or higher, according to people familiar with the discussions; the amount may vary depending on whether the rights for both tournaments are included.

data.description: According to Jin10, at the 2:30 close, the Shanghai gold futures main contract fell 1.45% to 794 yuan per gram, the Shanghai silver futures main contract declined 1.25% to 10,671 yuan per kilogram, and the SC crude oil futures main contract rose 2.84% to 593 yuan per barrel.

data.title: STOCKS | European Shares Extend Losing Streak to Four Days, Longest Since August
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, the Stoxx Europe 600 fell 0.9%, extending its decline to a fourth day and marking its longest losing streak since August. Defensive sectors weighed on the index, with food and beverages, personal care, health care and real estate among the biggest decliners. Investors awaited Anthropic PBC’s trading debut following its major IPO.

Technology shares initially rose on optimism surrounding Anthropic but turned lower late in the afternoon, tracking declines in U.S. stocks as AMD fell sharply.

In recent weeks, European stocks have outperformed U.S. indexes as concerns about the scale of AI spending have weighed on investor sentiment. Investors have shifted toward Europe, where banks, industrials and energy producers have greater weight, to reduce their exposure to technology stocks.

“Anthropic starting to trade is good news, but it does not remove the risks currently present, whether macro risks or AI-related risks,” said Neil Birrell, chief investment officer at Premier Miton. “Short-term indicators have been improving, but risk aversion remains dominant.”

data.title: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam Upgrade Could Slip to May 2027 Amid Compatibility Concerns
data.description:
Ethereum’s Glamsterdam upgrade could be delayed until May 2027 if developers revise its specifications to address smart contract compatibility risks. According to Cointelegraph, the possibility was discussed at Thursday’s All Core Developers meeting, where participants weighed keeping the current design against changes that could reduce risks for some contracts but potentially disrupt others. Glamsterdam is a planned Ethereum hard fork intended to increase network capacity and efficiency. In October, blockchain security firm ChainSecurity warned that proposed gas-pricing changes could disrupt existing smart contracts and potentially expose them to exploitation. Developers subsequently postponed the Hoodi testnet fork, which had been scheduled for Oct. 26. The concerns focus on gas repricing proposals EIP-8037 and EIP-8038. Researchers identified 13 real-world examples of contracts that could be affected in October, while a November investigation examined eight smart contract invariants that might be disrupted. At Thursday’s meeting, developers said the Ethereum Foundation, ChainSecurity and security firm Dedaub had contacted at least 50 affected companies. Three projects were deemed high impact, with fixes completed or expected by mid-December; medium-impact projects reported timelines extending to Jan. 10. One developer cautioned that changes to specifications could break other invariants that developers had not yet identified.

Under the existing specifications, Glamsterdam could activate on mainnet as early as mid-January 2027. However, if developers wait until January to decide whether to make changes, activation could move to late February or early March. Adopting modifications could push the upgrade further, to April or May, and developers have not reached a decision. Separately, Ethereum developers are considering reducing the scope of Hegotá, the network’s next planned hard fork, to accelerate its transition to post-quantum cryptography. During the meeting, participants discussed postponing some Ethereum Improvement Proposals to prioritize post-quantum features. Several developers argued that narrowing the upgrade’s scope would have limited value unless it also shortened the rollout timeline. Participants also raised compatibility concerns about EIP-8151, a proposal intended to protect accounts moving to post-quantum security. A preliminary review found that a potentially large number of existing smart contracts could be affected, creating uncertainty about including the proposal in Hegotá. Developers made no decision on the fork’s scope. Client teams are expected to provide their positions before further discussions in two weeks.

data.title: 60% of U.S. Crypto Owners Plan to Buy More, Outpacing Stock and ETF Owners
data.description:
Sixty percent of U.S. crypto owners plan to add to their holdings over the next 12 months, ahead of ETF owners (56%) and stock owners (52%). Charles Schwab’s 2026 survey found that bonds and mutual funds trailed at 42% and 41%, respectively, according to BeInCrypto. Long-term growth (36%) and diversification (33%) were the leading reasons for owning or wanting crypto, and half of current owners view it as an add-on to stocks and bonds. A third of millennials own crypto, compared with 8% of baby boomers, while 64% of millennials plan to buy more. The poll, commissioned from Logica Research, was not weighted and its crypto results were based on 413 owners.

Schwab opened direct crypto trading to eligible retail clients in October and charges a 0.75% fee per trade. Clients can buy Bitcoin and Ethereum; Schwab added Solana (SOL), Avalanche (AVAX) and Chainlink (LINK) on Nov. 9. Its 2025 annual report estimated that clients held about 20% of the U.S. market for spot crypto exchange-traded products. Morgan Stanley launched E*Trade crypto trading at 0.5% per trade, and Schwab plans to bring crypto trading to advisors in 2027. Among Americans who know of crypto, 52% call it high risk and 32% say it is not a legitimate asset. Non-owners cite scams (48%), lack of understanding (39%) and thin regulation (34%).

data.title: AI | Altimeter's Pauline Yang Says Anthropic IPO Is Just the Beginning
data.description: Altimeter’s Pauline Yang views Anthropic’s IPO as “Day One” for the AI company, ahead of its Nasdaq listing, Bloomberg reported. She discussed why Altimeter added to its Anthropic position in the offering and how improving compute economics changed its investment thesis. Yang sees room for both Anthropic and OpenAI to become multi-trillion-dollar companies.
